title: Early promoters George Moni and August Jackson
summary: Prompted by an old ad for Roy Milton, Tex describes promoters George Moni and August Jackson, the first gospel concert promoter.

bands.name: Roy Milton and His Solid Senders

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Then, you know, looking at this old newspaper, I'm thinking about a guy playing the Egyptian room, Labor's Union Hall, Sunday night, Roy Milton, with the Solid Senators. In fact, he just died here about three years ago with Camille Howard and Lily Greenwood, two top female vocalists. She was under the promotion of George Moni. Now, George Moni was a, I didn't know him not too well, but George Moni promoted quite a few shows in and around the city of New Orleans. And he was very, well he had a little money, he had his own businesses, and he had pretty good connections at that time. And he and, I'm thinking August Jackson was an I think, I wanted to, I was supposed to do an interview with August Jackson, but he reminds me of John Russo by not releasing newspapers. Jackson don't even want to be interviewed and talk about it, yesteryear, but yet he spent a lot of money. And he brought in many of the big names before Rook Roberts, and before anybody else I could think of in the history of promotion in the city of New Orleans. And he's 80-something years of age today, and now he's very active, retired, and he lives back here on Carrollton Avenue. He had his own businesses, and in fact he started promoting some of the, he was the first gospel concert promoter in the city of New Orleans that I could think of in his day. And I'm going to have to sneak up on him one day and bring a tape recorder in my pocket some kind of way, and try to talk with him.
